_description: Design point of the default 1F1C target: Laleni et al., 'A High-Efficiency Charge-Domain CIM 1F1C Macro Using 2-bit FeFET Cells for DNN Processing', IEEE JXCDC 2024. Every value has its source in _provenance. The SPICE scripts (targets/1fefet1c/spice/) read this file; 'reported_results' are Laleni's outputs, kept only to check our simulations against, never used as inputs.

adc.type: SAR, single-ended, conventional switching, bootstrapped sampling switch, input buffer

_provenance.architecture: Sec. III: each cell is one FeFET (RMU) with its own CMoM (WMU); the FeFET loads into the CMoM of the same cell, so RMU and WMU are coupled per cell
_provenance.process.node_nm: Sec. V: 'designed and simulated in 28-nm process technology'; FeFETs fabricated in 28 nm HKMG (Sec. III-A, Fig. 5)
_provenance.process.vdd_V: Sec. V: 'The supply voltage is chosen as VDD = 1 V'
_provenance.array.rows, array.cols: Sec. IV: '128 x 128 array of 1F1C cells'
_provenance.cell.bits_per_cell: Title, Sec. III-C: 2-bit FeFET cell, four Vth states
_provenance.cell.cmom_fF: Sec. IV and V: 'CMoM is selected as 1.3 fF'
_provenance.cell.vth_states_V: Sec. V: 'Vth1 is 0.3 V, Vth2 is 0.6 V, Vth3 is 0.9 V, and Vth4 ... is 1.2 V' (also Fig. 10(a))
_provenance.cell.vth_states_linear_V: Sec. IV, Fig. 10(b): alternative write scheme [1.2, 0.7, 0.4, 0.1 V] for uniform VBL steps
_provenance.clock.freq_MHz: Sec. V: 'The sampling frequency (Fs) of the operation is 20 MHz'
_provenance.clock.column_phase_cycles: Sec. III-B, Fig. 4: three phases (reset, multiply, accumulate). multiply (FeFET -> CMoM load) = 1 cycle: Sec. V, the FeFET 'is read in one cycle'; supported by SPICE (results/column.json -> fet_to_cap): the stored level has no settling point (it keeps rising ~logarithmically while WL is high), so the load time is the WL pulse width; at one cycle the four levels are distinct and evenly spaced, and longer pulses only let charge leak into the off ('0') state. reset and accumulate durations are not stated; one cycle each is our assumption (accumulate settles in 8.9 ns, results/column.json -> kappa)
_provenance.adc.type: Sec. IV: 'a conventional 7-bit SAR ADC with a bootstrap sampling switch'; 'an extra buffer is needed to drive this circuit'; Sec. V: 'conventional switching, since a single-ended SAR ADC is preferred'
_provenance.adc.cycles_per_conversion: Sec. V: 'eight cycles are needed to quantize the result by this ADC'
_provenance.adc.vrefp_V, adc.vrefn_V: Sec. V: 'Vrefp = 0.5 V and Vrefn = 0 V'
_provenance.adc.buffer_bias_uA: Our design: the input buffer's bias current, the bias the ADC and MAC results use (spice/adc/run_full.py bias sweep, results/adc.json bias_sweep; Laleni gives no bias)
_provenance.write: Sec. III-C: write-verify; HVT reset with -5 V for 500 ns, then 1.4 V pulses for 200 ns, increased in 40 mV steps with read-verify until the target Vth
_provenance.reported_results.cpar_fF: Sec. IV/V: 'Cpar = 75 fF' for 128 rows (our NVSim cell height is fitted to it, see 1f1c.cell)
_provenance.reported_results.kappa: Sec. V: 'the input range drops to 69%'
_provenance.reported_results.adc_enob_bits, adc_wald: Sec. V: 'ENOB ... 6.4 bits', 'Walden FoM of the ADC is 26 fJ/conversion'
_provenance.reported_results.bl_charging_power_nW: Sec. V: 'BL charging power is 0.86 nW with the expected value of weight as (VDD/2)'
_provenance.reported_results.cifar10_vgg8_accuracy_p: Sec. V: VGG-8 on CIFAR-10 with NeuroSim, 89%
